explanation: The empty-keys shortcut must come first: an empty list means there is nothing to walk, so data itself is the answer, and it must be checked before current is even set up. current has to be initialized to data before the loop reads it. Inside the loop, isinstance(current, dict) must be checked before key not in current — the "or" short-circuits, so if current were something like an int, testing membership on it directly would raise a TypeError. Only once both checks pass can current safely advance to current[key], and only after the whole loop finishes without an early return does the final current hold the answer.
